new_statements.quote: in Cholón the last syllable was normally stressed, or, as Pedro de la Mata observes, “[...] no tiene mas [acentos] que uno en la ultima siylaba, assi en nombres como en verbos” (p. 79). | In his paragraph about the accent, de la Mata mentions that in Cholón stress is word-final, and he gives the following examples: (159) mallâ (2979) ‘something raw’ (160) llín (2980) ‘something green’ (161) llêz (2982) ‘alfalfa’ (162) patôx (2981) ‘remnant’, ‘residue’ (p. 106). | Del acento [1: en la ultima siylaba] 2979 mallâ : cosa cruda 2980 llín : cosa verde 2981 patôx : desecho 2982 llêz : rastrojo y lucerna pequeña [2: en la penultima en algunos tiempos] 2983 cuchiEle mectan, el-l milangova / mallà mul[l]uppoEva? : eres puerco que comes yuca cruda? (p. 503)
new_statements.translation: Spanish parts: '[...] it has no more [accents] than one, on the last syllable, in nouns as well as in verbs' (the dissertation's own footnote renders it: 'there is only one accent, on the last syllable, in nouns as well as in verbs'). 'On the accent [1: on the last syllable] ... mallâ : raw thing; llín : green thing; patôx : leftover; llêz : stubble and small alfalfa. [2: on the penultimate in some tenses] ... : are you a pig, that you eat raw manioc?'
new_statements.citation: Alexander-Bakkerus, Astrid. 2005. Eighteenth-Century Cholón. Utrecht: LOT (LOT 120). 533 pp. [NOT in the listed works; full text already held by the project in our check folder from 2026-09-16, re-downloaded from lotpublications.nl; it contains Alexander-Bakkerus's transcription of de la Mata's accent chapter and her analysis of ALC stress marking]
new_statements.locator: p. 79 (section 4.2.7.5, with footnote translation); pp. 106-107 (section 4.5 'The use of the diacritics'); p. 503 (Appendix, transcription of ALC 'Libro quinto.. Del acento', entries 2979-2983); p. 521 (transcription conventions for 1990s rememberer data)
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: the PDF's metadata 533 pages, title 'Proefschrift Astrid Alexander.. 11 oktober 2005'; printed page numbers are page headers and coincide with PDF page indices, so the locators are exact. p. 79 (PDF 79, section 4.2.7.5): 'in Cholón the last syllable was normally stressed, or, as Pedro de la Mata observes, "[..] no tiene mas [acentos] que uno en la ultima siylaba, assi en nombres como en verbos"' verbatim, with footnote (numbered 13 in the footnote block) '"[..] there is only one accent, on the last syllable, in nouns as well as in verbs"'. p. 106 (section 4.5): 'In his paragraph about the accent, de la Mata mentions that in Cholón stress is word-final, and he gives the following examples: (…
new_statements.relation_note: Catalog final stress = fixed final; de la Mata's rule as transcribed and analysed here is stress on the last syllable in nouns and verbs, i.e. the same placement. Adds detail: marking conventions, a possible penultimate variant 'in some tenses', later-hand grave accents, and the modern rememberer data where non-final accent is occasionally marked. This work was not in the 'works' list; it is reported as an extra because it carries the only actual stress statement found.
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress falls on the last syllable, in nouns and verbs alike (de la Mata's own rule, endorsed by Alexander-Bakkerus: 'in Cholón the last syllable was normally stressed'). The ALC marks it with a circumflex on a/e/o/u and an acute/stroke on i. De la Mata's accent chapter has a second sub-heading, editorially summarised as 'en la penultima en algunos tiempos' (penultimate in some verb tenses), illustrated by one sentence.
new_statements.exceptions: (a) De la Mata's accent chapter has a second heading, editorially bracketed as '[2: en la penultima en algunos tiempos]' (penultimate in some tenses), with one example sentence (2983) containing mallà with a grave accent (p. 503). (b) p. 107: 'Occasionally, a grave accent may have the function of a stress mark: in the lexical items mallà ‘something raw’ and quexùm ‘nose’.. it may have been added by the later hand.' (c) p. 106: the circumflex may alternatively mark a separately pronounced vowel / glottal stop rather than stress (âamoctan). (d) p. 521, on the 1990s data from the rememberers Aurelia Gutiérrez and José Santos Chapa: 'accent by means of an acute accent. Note that accent is only indicated when it is not word-final' -- i.e. some non-final accents occur in the modern rememberer data, word-final being the unmarked default.
new_statements.identity_note: All statements concern the 18th-century Cholón of the Arte de la lengua cholona (de la Mata 1748, copied by Gerónimo Clota 1772 at San Buenaventura del Valle, Huallaga; British Library ms. Add. 25,322), plus Alexander-Bakkerus's 1996 recordings of two rememberers (Aurelia Gutiérrez, José Santos Chapa) from the same area. No other variety is described.

audit.reasoning: The classification (fixed final, dominant not strict) rests on the only full grammar of this extinct language (Alexander-Bakkerus 2005, 533 pp), which relays the 1748 grammarian's explicit rule ('only one accent, on the last syllable, in nouns as well as in verbs') and his stress diacritics, and is corroborated by the author's own rememberer recordings (final stress unmarked by default). Full text was not yet obtained before; it is now downloaded (LOT open access) and the quotation is confirmed verbatim at p.79 (locator should read p.79, sec. 4.2.7.5, not p.80; second passage pp.106-107 sec. 4.5 confirmed).
